learning_outcomes.text: Apply the principles of thermodynamics and conservation equations to the analysis of operation and efficiency calculations of nozzles, diffusers, steam power cycles, gas power cycles, and thermal engines.

Calculate the basic operating parameters (stages and pressure drops, volumetric efficiency, isoentropic/polytropic efficiency) in turbomachinery and thermal machine components and recognize their importance in the design process.

Recognize different technical alternatives, components, and process schemes applicable to conventional electric power generation plants, their basic characteristics, and the efficiency of the processes they promote.
Describe, differentiate, and select equipment for the assembly of thermal machines and engines, including turbomachinery and internal combustion engines.
Calculate the energy and power production and consumption capacity of thermal machines and installations and the effect of the design of their main components on this capacity.
Determine the environmental and health impact of thermal machines and engines and the main methods aimed at preventing it.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans, and other similar tasks.
Ability to manage specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards.

syllabus_topics: Topic 1. The thermal machine, general concepts
BLOCK II. COMPRESSIBLE FLOW IN DUCTS
Topic 2: Analysis of nozzles and diffusers
BLOCK III. THERMAL ENGINES BASED ON THERMAL TURBOMACHINERY
Topic 5: Combined Cycle and Cogeneration Power Plants
Topic 6: Aeronautical applications of the gas turbine engine
BLOCK IV. THERMAL ENGINES BASED ON RECIPROCATING INTERNAL COMBUSTION ENGINES (RICE)
BLOCK V. ENVIRONMENTAL IMPLICATIONS AND FUTURE PERSPECTIVES
Topic 10. Environmental impact and future of thermal machines

assessment_methods.method: Written exam (theory and problems from Topics 1 to 10)

assessment_rules: The general evaluation model is continuous assessment. No single evaluation activity can exceed 60% of the global grade. Non-re-evaluable activities cannot exceed 40% of the global grade. The written exam, practical report submission, and practical exam require a minimum score of 5 and are re-evaluable. The submission of proposed problems is not re-evaluable and has no minimum score. Students who do not pass or do not attend the ordinary call can take the extraordinary call for unpassed re-evaluable activities.
